name: clipping the church

attributes.attribute: old holy place echoed in the rite
time when the yews were cut

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Clipping the church is a British rite. In some English villages, children moved in a ring around the churchyard and touched, or clipped, the church walls as they went. The church often rose on an old holy place, so this rite echoed a time when people touched the stones of a stone ring. In the Cotswolds the rite came in autumn, when the yew trees in the churchyard were trimmed around the equinox.
